title: confined_external is unusable for single-crate packages: manifest is never in allowed_in
description:
`confined_external` checks two signals: use-statements and the Cargo.toml `[dependencies]` manifest. For a single-crate package the manifest signal makes the constraint unsatisfiable — `Cargo.toml` is by definition not one of the source files listed in `allowed_in`, so the constraint emits a permanent blocking violation that no code change can clear.

Reproduced on yojana. This constraint:

```toml
[[constraint]]
kind = "confined_external"
crates = ["rusqlite"]
allowed_in = ["src/db.rs", "src/error.rs"]
severity = "blocking"
```

yields:

```
external crate outside confinement: Cargo.toml -> rusqlite via manifest
dependency (allowed only in [src/db.rs, src/error.rs])
from_path: Cargo.toml
```

The use-statement signal is correct and useful — only db.rs and error.rs import rusqlite, which is exactly the single-point-of-contact invariant worth enforcing. The manifest signal is what breaks it.

The manifest check is presumably there to catch a dependency declared but not yet imported. That intent is sound for a *workspace* (crate A declaring a dep that only crate B should use), but wrong for the package that declares the dep for its own use.

Proposed fix: exempt the manifest entry when `allowed_in` contains at least one path belonging to the package that declares the dependency. Alternative if that is too subtle: an explicit `check_manifest = false` opt-out, though a footgun that every single-crate user must discover and disable is a worse default.

The constraint is currently commented out in yojana/.sutra/rules.toml with a pointer here; re-add once fixed.

acceptance_criteria.text: A confined_external constraint on a single-crate package whose allowed_in paths are inside that package does not report the manifest as a violation
The manifest signal still fires in a multi-crate workspace when a non-owning member declares the confined dependency
Re-adding the rusqlite confined_external to yojana/.sutra/rules.toml produces zero violations
Regression test covers both the single-crate and workspace cases

decisions.decision: Decide confinement ownership by aligning the allowed_in glob's components against package directories, not by prefix arithmetic on the glob's literal head
decisions.rationale: The literal head of crates/*/src/db.rs is crates/, which is not a package directory, so a prefix rule exempted the workspace root (silently disabling a blocking rule) while still blocking the member that actually holds the path — inverting the fix. Component alignment resolves the wildcard segment against real packages. Ambiguity resolves toward not owning, because a wrong exemption is silent while a wrong report is visible and waivable.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Keep literal-prefix ownership and treat only unambiguous parent prefixes as owning — simpler, but it leaves allowed_in = ["**/client.rs"] unsatisfiable for the very single-package case the task is about.

decisions.decision: Guard and index both derive the package layout from a disk scan (package_dirs_including)
decisions.rationale: The guard's members-derived view omitted nested non-member packages, so it exempted a root dependency the index then reported — the guard stops predicting blocking audit findings. One discovery path removes the divergence class.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Align the index to declared [workspace].members instead; rejected because a package present on disk but undeclared still owns its own sources, and the index is the authority.

execution_record:
Fix is `manifest_owns_confinement` in src/constraints/external.rs: skip the manifest signal when the manifest's package owns an `allowed_in` path, ownership going to the deepest entry in `package_dirs_of` so a workspace root does not swallow a member's confinement paths. `check_manifest`/`check_pubspec` gained a `package_dirs` parameter; the index side derives it from the scanned manifests, the guard side from the root manifest's declared members (proposed content wins for the manifest under edit).

Applied through `match_external_where` applicability rather than filtering findings afterwards — sutra/296 established that post-filtering lets the exempt rule win first-match and shadow a narrower rule. Test `exempt_confinement_does_not_shadow_a_forbidden_external_rule` pins that.

Also collapsed two copies of glob literal-prefix extraction into `constraints::glob_literal_prefix`.

Rejected the `check_manifest = false` opt-out named in the description: a footgun every single-crate user must discover is a worse default than inferring ownership.

Verification: 1519 lib+integration tests pass, clippy clean on touched files; a scratch integration test ran the real yojana rules through `check_workspace_externals` and returned zero findings with the constraint re-added (yojana 4608602). The running sutra MCP server still holds the pre-fix binary — it picks the fix up on next restart.
root_cause: The manifest signal treated a `[dependencies]` entry as a violation site on the same footing as a source file, but a manifest path can never satisfy `allowed_in` — that field lists source paths. For a package whose confinement targets its own sources, the declaration that makes the confined import possible was itself reported, so the constraint had no satisfiable state.

context_refs.label: yojana adoption; constraint commented out with rationale

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review of a005b11 — verdict: needs-attention (both findings now fixed in 02e2708).

[high] Wildcarded allowed_in can exempt the wrong manifest (src/constraints/external.rs:175-183)
manifest_owns_confinement reduced each allowed_in pattern to the text before the first glob metacharacter, then assigned ownership by checking whether the manifest dir contains that literal prefix. For allowed_in = ["crates/*/src/db.rs"] and package dirs ["", "crates/api"], target became "crates/": the root manifest was treated as owning it (an empty dir contains everything, and no deeper package contains that parent prefix), while crates/api/Cargo.toml was NOT treated as owning it (crates/api does not contain "crates/"). Impact: a root package silently avoids a blocking manifest violation for a dep only member crates may use, and the actual member manifest still gets the unsatisfiable violation this commit is meant to remove.
Recommendation: do not infer ownership from the pre-glob literal prefix; evaluate the allowed_in glob against package dirs so wildcarded member segments resolve to the matching member package(s), or treat ambiguous parent-prefix patterns as non-owning. Add regression tests for crates/*/src/... and */src/... patterns.

[medium] Cargo guard and index derive different ownership layouts (src/constraints/check.rs:1049-1060)
The guard built package_dirs from Cargo.toml plus [workspace].members manifests; the index built its dirs from a filesystem scan of every Cargo.toml. With a nested non-member vendor/client/Cargo.toml and allowed_in = ["vendor/client/src/**"], the guard omits vendor/client, treats the root as owning the confinement path, and exempts the root dependency — while the index includes vendor/client, assigns ownership there, and reports the root manifest. Undermines the guard as a predictor of blocking audit findings.
Recommendation: use one shared Cargo package discovery function for both guard and index. Add a guard-vs-index regression with a nested non-member package under an allowed_in path.

Next steps (both done in 02e2708): fix ownership inference for wildcarded package segments; unify package-dir derivation, with regressions exercising the public guard/index entry points rather than check_manifest with hand-built dirs.
